Chapter Seven: Work, Vocation, and the Soul’s Calling.
Let’s talk about work for a second. Most of us see it as just a way to pay the bills, build a career, or maybe hit those markers of success we’ve been taught to chase. But have you ever felt a deeper longing beneath all that? That quiet wish for work to actually mean something—to fit who you are, and to light you up inside?
The world, honestly, doesn’t make it easy to reflect on these things. We’re encouraged to be productive, efficient, and rack up achievements. But what happens when you wake up one day and realize you’re just... going through the motions?
Picture this: there’s a man in his thirties, absolutely successful by most standards. But lately, every day feels like a carbon copy of the last. He starts to wonder—Is this all there is? He remembers a time when work used to excite him, when it felt like an extension of who he was. That sense of purpose, though, now feels so far away.
Then, one weekend, he volunteers at a local community center, helping kids with art projects. And something shifts. He feels joy and connection—feelings he hasn’t had in years. It’s like a small flame gets rekindled.
Most of us don’t notice just how much our work shapes who we are. The soul, though, keeps asking for something real—work that’s authentic, that lets us be creative, grow, and serve others. That doesn’t mean you have to chase after the perfect job, or wait for a grand calling to show up. Sometimes, it’s about bringing a bit of soulfulness into whatever you’re already doing.
Think about this: maybe it’s finding meaning in the little tasks. Or building relationships with your coworkers. Or just facing each day’s challenges with curiosity instead of dread.
Here’s another story. There’s a woman working in a high-pressure office, constantly drained by the demands. She starts taking short walks during her lunch break, just noticing the trees and the shifting light. Those brief pauses help her reconnect with herself. Slowly, she brings more of her true self into her job—sharing her ideas, supporting her coworkers, and finding satisfaction in the process, not just the end result.
What she learns is powerful: vocation isn’t just about what you do, but how you do it. The soul gets nourished by work that lines up with your values and passions. But it can also find meaning in the ordinary, if you approach it with care and intention.
Take the retiree who wasn’t sure how to fill all his new free time. He starts volunteering at a local animal shelter. The work is simple, but it brings him a sense of purpose and connection he didn’t expect. He realizes the soul’s calling isn’t always about grand, dramatic gestures. Sometimes, it’s in those small acts of service—just showing up, and making a difference, even if it’s modest.
Most of us fall into the habit of separating work from the rest of life, treating it like a burden to get through. But the soul asks for something else: integration. A way of living where work, relationships, and personal growth all connect.
If you bring a little soulfulness to your work, you might be surprised at the meaning and satisfaction you can find—even in the most everyday tasks.
So, here’s what it really comes down to. The journey toward soulful work isn’t about landing the perfect job. It’s about listening to those longings inside, and weaving them into your daily life. When you approach work with care, creativity, and real purpose, it can actually become a source of growth and fulfillment.
